about: Site updates shown on /changes. One entry per working session, a sentence or two: changes within 2 hours of the newest entry's time go into it (and its time moves to now); otherwise a new entry goes on top. It does not have to cover everything. See CLAUDE.md.

updates.text: Log a day now opens on “Where are you riding?”, with nearby and recent parks one tap away. Pages share one look now, and categories show the rides you’ve ridden in bold, the rest in grey, and closed ones marked defunct.

Coaster Hub has a new look: a painted park skyline on every page, bolder headlines, a home page with your last park day, next milestone and friends as tiles, and coaster pages that show each stat against the record holder. Coaster pages also have a Log this ride button.

Coaster Hub's coaster data now comes from open sources (Coasterpedia, Wikidata and OpenStreetMap) instead of RCDB, with a new Sources page in the sitemap showing how many stats come from each. Some stats are blank until an open source fills them in, and every rider's credits and rankings are unchanged.

Profiles have a card for this year so far: new credits, rides, park days, parks, your biggest day and most-visited park. Coaster pages show their stats in a band across the page, with relocated rides listing their Past locations as a timeline.

Coming back to a park day on Log now shows what you've already ridden that day, with new credits marked, and Home's "You're at" card looks like a park ticket. Your count on Home ticks up to its new number after you log, and activity rows have coaster-themed icons.

Profiles have a cleaner Among friends section and a Lost credits list of rides you've done that closed or moved. Rankings gained find-in-your-list, an All / Ridden / Not ridden filter on Global, and your parks ranked from your list.
Rides already on your count from before you started logging dates are no longer marked New in Recent visits or On this day.
On this day on your profile now lists each past visit on that date: the year, the park and the rides you took, with new credits marked.
The "Can't decide" button when ranking a coaster is now "About the same", which says what it does: puts the new ride right below the one you're comparing it with.
Coasters that haven't opened yet say "Under construction" in yellow until their opening day. The Rankings page no longer lists every rider's ranking under the Global list.
Categories page is cleaner: no note under each Coaster Hub category, and a shorter intro.
Global rankings now get stricter on their own as more people rank, so a few fans can't outrank a crowd; today's order doesn't change.
You can now sign in with your username or your email.
Rankings pages now just say whose rankings they are, without the extra tagline.

Log a day is cleaner: one + per coaster until you ride it, the date as a chip at the top, closed rides folded away, and the save bar opens the day's list. Sign-up also won't take an email address as a username and limits new accounts per connection.
Profiles no longer scroll sideways on a phone when "On this day" lists a coaster at a park with a long name.

Racing coasters like Superman: Escape From Krypton now show as one row in the Global rankings and on profiles' top ten, at the better side's place, and opening the row shows each side. Other riders' pages also no longer show old numbers saved from your last visit.
Resetting a forgotten password works again: the Set password button on the reset page did nothing when pressed, and now saves the new password and signs you in.

Pages open faster on phones: scripts and the big coaster lists are kept on your phone instead of being re-downloaded on every tap, and Home shows your count straight away. In the iPhone app, the bottom tabs switch without sliding and Back slides like a native app.

You can now delete your account, report or block a rider from the ⋯ on their page, and share any profile with the new share button; Terms of Use and a Privacy Policy are linked at the bottom of every page. On computers, the light/dark toggle is back in the top bar.

On phones, Coaster Hub now feels like an app: pages slide in and out, swipe or long-press a coaster to log a ride, and rides logged with no signal send themselves once you're back online. You can also delete or edit any day you've logged, right from your profile.

Relocated rides are now linked as one credit with their history on each coaster page, and traveling shows are labeled Fair operator with their own filter on /parks. On profiles, the rides only you have ridden among your friends are now listed by park and location.

New Trip planner maps your trip with new credits per park for you and any friends, and Compare puts you head to head with a friend. Profiles now show where you rank among your friends, and manufacturer pages list every coaster they built.
The Updates section on Home now includes what your friends did, not just everyone else.
New How rankings work page explains how Rank more places a ride and how every list becomes the Global score. It's linked from the bottom of your list on Rankings and from the Global list's heading.

Coaster pages now show when a former name was in use, like Canyon Cruiser's "Formerly Canyon Blaster (1999 – June 5, 2026)". New categories for Zamperla Family Gravity Coasters and Miner Mikes, and "Manufacturers" replaces "makers" across the site.

Global rankings now use a score out of 100 weighted by each rider's credits, and ranking got a Can't decide button and new categories that place as one. Another rider's list now shows how much you agree with them and your biggest split.
Import takes a Google Sheets link, matches near-misses for you, and lets you add a missing ride or park right from the list.

On your profile the Account menu now sits beside the rider switcher, with Log a day and your rankings next to your stats on a phone. Other riders' profiles no longer show how many coasters you've both ridden.

Park, manufacturer, model, location and coaster pages now share one layout, /log has one search box and keeps staged rides through a reload, and Explore leads with Parks and Coasters. Every Global list now shows the average with your own place under it in grey, and Credits and Map open with your name and count like your profile.

Coaster, park, manufacturer, model and location pages were reworked: your verdict up top, Global rankings first, rider pictures, ones you still need listed first, and long lists that fold to Show all. Signed in, the home page opens on your own count, and dark mode is a deeper night blue.

New /users page lists everyone A–Z with site-wide totals, and the home page now shows the top ten with a link to it. Phone lists and opened rows are tighter, and profiles have a rankings button for everyone.

Page headers now carry a little park skyline — a Magnum-style coaster in side view with its train cresting the hill, a Ferris wheel, a drop tower and swings — lit up at night on a deep navy, and on a sky-blue gradient by day. Dark mode is navy instead of grey throughout.

Every coaster, park and model list on the site — including your credits and recent visits — now shares one row style that matches /rankings, with a Mine / Global ranking on manufacturer, model and location pages. Rides pulled out of a category show how far above or below it they sit.

New riders get a two-minute setup that ends with a head-to-head top ten, and Rank more makes ranking the rest easy. Rankings can be filtered by model, and Manufacturers is now A–Z with each maker's stats opening right in the list.
A day copied to a friend now shows in the feed a minute after the original.
Relocated rides now count as one credit with one page, search forgives typos and knows park initials, and the homepage and profile got tidier.
